questions.q: How is a coefficient in a multiple regression correctly read?
options: The correlation between that feature and the target
The predicted change in the target per one-unit increase in that feature, holding the other features fixed
The share of variance explained by that feature alone
The p-value of the feature
questions.explain: Each coefficient is the change in the prediction for a one-unit increase in its feature with all other features held constant. It is not a correlation or a variance share.

questions.q: With two features, what shape does the fitted multiple regression model have?
options: A single straight line
A flat plane
A parabola
A decision tree
questions.explain: One feature gives a line, two features give a plane, and three or more give a hyperplane that works the same way but cannot be drawn.

questions.q: In the lesson, square footage alone scored a test R-squared of 0.914 and all three features scored 0.952. What does this show?
options: Adding features always raises test performance
The test set was too small to trust
The model memorized the training data
Age contributed independent information that improved predictions on unseen data
questions.explain: Both scores are on the same held-out test set, so the improvement reflects real signal in age, not memorization. It does not follow that adding features always helps.

questions.q: Square footage and bedrooms correlate at 0.83, and the fitted beds coefficient drifted from the value built into the data. What is this problem called?
options: Data leakage
Underfitting
Multicollinearity
Class imbalance
questions.explain: When features overlap, the model cannot cleanly assign credit between them, so individual coefficients become unstable even if predictions stay accurate.

questions.q: What should you do with a categorical feature such as neighborhood before fitting linear regression?
options: Encode it into numbers, for example with one-hot columns and drop_first=True
Feed the text directly to LinearRegression
Delete the column because regression can't use categories
Replace it with its alphabetical rank
questions.explain: Regression needs numeric input. One-hot encoding creates 0/1 columns, and dropping one avoids redundancy. Alphabetical rank would impose a meaningless order.
